verdict.rationale: Svelte's docs say components are written in HTML, CSS and JavaScript. State is a plain variable you update normally, and CSS goes in a standard <style> block scoped to the component. A community user also reports Svelte as much simpler than React. However, the docs show framework-specific concepts on top of standard syntax ($derived, $effect, $state.raw, $derived.by, getter-function patterns), and one user describes it as a JS 'superset' that caused IDE-support friction. Missing for 10: evidence that the rune and template additions stay minimal, independent hands-on corroboration of the low learning curve, and tooling that treats the syntax as standard.
